title: Beef, short loin, porterhouse steak, separable lean only, trimmed to 1/8" fat, select, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Porterhouse steak from the short loin of beef is a large cut that includes both the tenderloin and a portion of the strip steak. This version contains only the lean portion, with excess fat trimmed to 1/8 inch. It is classified as a “select” grade and is supplied raw.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A porterhouse combines two different muscles: the tenderloin and the strip steak.
The name “Porterhouse” dates back to the 19th‑century Porter House hotel in New York, where the cut was first popularized.
The lean portion typically makes up 70‑80 % of the total weight of the steak.
A thin fat cap (marbling) contributes to juiciness and flavor, but here it is minimized for a leaner product.
Raw beef should be stored at 0 °C‑4 °C and used within 2‑3 days.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Porterhouse steak provides about 22 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: After trimming to 1/8" fat, the steak contains only 4‑5 g of fat per 100 g, suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef is rich in vitamin B12, niacin (B3) and riboflavin (B2), which aid energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Essential minerals
items.content: The cut supplies iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood formation, immunity and bone health.

items.title: Creatine
items.content: Natural creatine in beef can help improve physical performance and endurance.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Raw beef may harbor pathogenic bacteria such as E. coli or Salmonella; proper cooking is essential.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: High purine content
items.content: People with gout or elevated uric acid should limit intake.

items.title: Sodium considerations
items.content: If the steak is pre‑salted, account for its sodium contribution to the overall diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Porterhouse steak is best cooked over high heat – grill, cast‑iron grill pan, or broiler. Aim for an internal temperature of 55‑60 °C for medium‑rare. Let the steak rest at room temperature for 20‑30 minutes before cooking for even doneness. Serve with vegetables, potatoes, or a light sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw beef in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for no more than 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C, where it retains quality for up to 6 months. Thaw frozen steak in the refrigerator, not at room temperature.
